subject: maths
question: A solution of 100 litres has a 60% salt concentration. How many litres of water must be added to reduce the concentration to 40%, and then how much pure salt must be added to bring the concentration back to 50%?

options.text: Add 50 L of water, then 30 L of salt
Add 90 L of water, then 70 L of salt
Add 70 L of water, then 30 L of salt
Add 50 L of water, then 10 L of salt

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial salt = 60% of 100 L = 60 L. When water is added, the salt quantity remains constant.

To reduce concentration to 40%, the new total volume must be = 60 × (100 ÷ 40) = 150 L.

Water added = 150 − 100 = 50 L. The mixture now has 90 L water and 60 L salt.

To increase concentration back to 50%, the amount of salt must equal the amount of water.

Since water is 90 L, salt must also become 90 L. Pure salt to add = 90 − 60 = 30 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 L of water, then 30 L of salt.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial solution = 100 L

Initial salt concentration = 60%

**Concept Used:**

When water is added, the amount of salt remains constant. When pure salt is added, the amount of water remains constant.
